feedback.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)=-\sqrt{3}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +\frac{n\pi }{3},
$$

 
where $n$ is any integer. What could be the value of $a?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{9}+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=-\frac{1}{9}.$
